issues.legal_issue: An involuntary transfer made after the relevant cutoff is subject to the same conditions as a voluntary transfer before it may be excluded from a tenure-holder’s surplus land calculation.
material_facts: A creditor obtained a court-ordered auction sale of a large area of the tenure-holder’s land after the ceiling proceedings had begun.
The sale was made to the decree-holders for a small sum in relation to the area sold.
The purchasers did not establish that the sale was bona fide and for adequate consideration.
issues.conclusion: The auction sale was not exempt from the rules governing transfers merely because it was involuntary; it could be excluded from the surplus calculation only if the required conditions were proved.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5(6) of the Uttar Pradesh Imposition of Ceiling on Land Holdings Act, 1960 requires post-cutoff transfers to be ignored unless the transfer satisfies the proviso, including good faith, adequate consideration and an irrevocable instrument, and is not benami or for the immediate or deferred benefit of the tenure-holder or family. Explanation II places the burden of proving the exception on the party claiming it. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: ceiling_proceeding and transfer_after_cutoff and involuntary_transfer and not qualifying_transfer_proven

predicates.ceiling_proceeding: A proceeding to determine a landholder’s surplus land was underway.
predicates.transfer_after_cutoff: The landholder’s land was transferred after the date from which later transfers were subject to scrutiny in the surplus calculation.
predicates.involuntary_transfer: The land was transferred through a process imposed by a court rather than by the landholder’s voluntary choice.
predicates.qualifying_transfer_proven: The party seeking to rely on the transfer established that it was bona fide, for adequate consideration, made under an irrevocable instrument, and neither benami nor for the landholder’s or family’s benefit.

issues.definition: When a post-cutoff involuntary transfer occurs in a ceiling proceeding and the party relying on it does not prove the qualifying conditions, the transfer is ignored in calculating surplus land.

issues.legal_issue: A transfer of land during the continuation of proceedings to determine surplus land is void even if it is involuntary and conducted under a court order.
material_facts: The auction sale took place while proceedings to determine the tenure-holder’s surplus land were pending.
The sale was conducted by an executing court to recover decretal sums.
The sale was confirmed and certificates were issued, but the transfer occurred during the pending ceiling proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The sale was void because it took place during the continuation of the surplus land proceedings, and the court order did not validate it.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5(8) of the Uttar Pradesh Imposition of Ceiling on Land Holdings Act, 1960, notwithstanding subsections (6) and (7), makes a transfer during the continuation of surplus land determination proceedings void. Its explanation identifies when those proceedings are deemed to commence and conclude. The Court held that the rule applies to involuntary as well as voluntary sales and that a civil court’s order cannot validate a sale that would defeat the ceiling law. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.ceiling_proceeding: A proceeding to determine a landholder’s surplus land was underway.
predicates.land_transfer_during_proceeding: Land held by the person whose surplus was being determined was transferred before that proceeding had concluded.

issues.definition: When land is transferred while a proceeding to determine the landholder’s surplus is underway, the transfer is void.
